name: Timna
overview: Timna was a female Edomite known primarily as the concubine of Eliphaz, son of Esau, and the sister of Lotan. Her identity is rooted in her tribal affiliation with the Edomites and her familial connection to notable figures in the Genesis genealogies. There are no additional notes expanding on her character or life.
namesAndTitles: The name Timna means "lot" or "portion," reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin as recorded in Genesis 36:12. This meaning does not indicate divine origin or special title but serves as a simple identifier within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Timna's relationships include being the concubine of Eliphaz, Esau's son, and the mother of Amalek, which is inferred from the text. She is also explicitly identified as the sister of Lotan. These connections place her within the Edomite lineage and link her to significant descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Timna's significance in Scripture lies in her role within the Edomite genealogies, particularly as the concubine of Eliphaz and the mother of Amalek, who becomes the ancestor of the Amalekites, a notable group in later biblical history. Her mention highlights the complex family relationships stemming from Esau and the formation of various tribes. Though not extensively detailed, her presence in the genealogical record underscores God's providential ordering of nations and peoples.
